messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] exporting to mapQTL format
messages.body_plain:
FYI - This problem comes from the data having all 4 genotypes AC, AD, BC, BD, and a few partially missing A-, B-, -C, -D.
Since my data is mostly complete, I can get around this via:

> for(chr in chrnames(cross_2write)) cross_2write$geno[[chr]]$data[cross_2write$geno[[chr]]$data>4]<-NA

On Friday, February 24, 2017 at 5:48:53 PM UTC-6, John Lovell wrote:
> Hi Karl,
> I am dealing the the same issue as Federico:
> ...
> write.cross(bad4way, filestem = "~/Downloads/bad4way", format = "mapqtl") Error: unrecognized segregation type at marker Chr01K_1008832
> ...
> Chr01K_1008832 is the 1st marker on the 1st chromosome and has a segregation pattern with the next marker that looks like this:
> > table(g2[,1], g2[,2])
>       1   2   3   4   7
>   1 117   1   2   0   1
>   2   3  94   0   3   0
>   3   2   1 101   4   0
>   4   0   1   1  99   0
>   5   0   0   1   0   0
>
> It seems that my genotype data is in order (I can pull together a map etc.), but clearly it isn't. I have spent a bunch of time trying to troubleshoot and can't figure it out. All markers in this population are ABxCD, phase-known with all four genotypes represented. Coding follows the read.cross guidelines, using this dictionary:
>
> matrix(c(NA,"--",
>                  1, "AC",
>                  2, "BC",
>                  3, "AD",
>                  4, "BD",
>                  5 , "A-",
>                  6 , "B-",
>                  7 , "-C",
>                  8 , "-D"), ncol = 2, byrow=T)
>
> I'm attaching an .rda file with of the 1st chromosome in case you can make some time to have a look.
> Any help is appreciated.
> John
>
>
>
>
>
> On Thursday, June 25, 2015 at 7:06:29 AM UTC-5, Karl Broman wrote:
> write.cross with format="mapqtl" only works for phase-known 4-way cross data.
>
> Your call to read.cross isn't really working properly. The genotypes vector for a 4-way cross needs to be a specific list of genotype codes, corresponding to these:
> 1 = AC, 2 = BC, 3 = AD, 4 = BD,
> 5 = A = AC or AD, 6 = B = BC or BD, 7 = C = AC or BC, 8 = D = AD or BD,
> 9 = AC or BD, 10 = AD or BC,
> 11 = not AC, 12 = not BC, 13 = not AD, 14 = not BD
>
> So the data object in R is not really what you want, and while it thinks this is a 4-way cross, R/qtl can't convert it into the MapQTL format.
>
> karl
>
> > On Jun 25, 2015, at 3:27 AM, Federico Calboli <f.ca...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > Hi All,
> >
> > I am trying to use R/qtl to export some data to mapQTL format (no, it is not for me, I'd just use R/qtl). In any case, I have data for an F1/F2 (309 F2 + the 2 F1, which are the two last lines of data). I have the data in 'csv' format, and I can read it in without a single problem by doing:
> >
> > dat = read.cross(format = 'csv', dir = '.', 'f1f2.csv', na.strings = 'NA', genotypes = c('AA','AC','AG','AT','CC','CG','CT','GG','GT','TT'), alleles=c('A','C','G','T'), estimate.map = FALSE)
> >
> > Unfortunately when I try to export it
> >
> > write.cross(dat, format = 'mapqtl', filestem = 'HB', chr = 1, digits = NULL)
> >
> > I get
> >
> > Error: unrecognized segregation type at marker 24319 on chromosome 1
> >
> > (there is at least 1 marker R/qtl does not like in every chromosome). I suspect that I might need to specify that the last 2 individuals are the F1 male and female. Alternatively I might have to remove them... In any case I'd be obliged if you could suggest what I can do to get the export done and over with...
> >
> > Cheers
> >
> > Federico
> >

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] Puzzled!! how to filter the data??
messages.body_plain:
Dear Prof Browman, you mentioned the removal of near monomorphic markers, is filtering at 0.01 or 1% minor allele frequency okay for nearly monomorphic or 0.05 (5% ) minor allele frequency?

Thanks.

On Wednesday, February 8, 2017 at 11:01:28 PM UTC-6, Karl Broman wrote:
> I would start by focusing on the progeny genotypes: omit markers that are monomorphic, or nearly monomorphic.
>
> I only have experience with RIL where the parents are inbred lines. I'm not sure immediately what to do with the case that the parents have heterozygosity. The simplest case to focus on is where the two parents are homozygous with different alleles, so you might just start with those markers.
>
> But are these RIL? My initial impression is that there's quite a lot of heterozygosity in the progeny lines. And segregation distortion.
>
> karl
>
>
> > On Feb 8, 2017, at 11:23 AM, Somnath Roy <sro...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > Hi!!
> > I'm trying to analyse a set of SNP data of a RIL population of rice. I've SNP data of 172 progenies and 2 parents. While filtering the data, I did complete the filter for missing for both parents, bad/questionable, missing SNP in >10 progenies. So my SNP reduced from 40894 to 37991. Now, I don't know which SNPs should be considered for analysis.
> > I have to discard SNPs those are 'homo (parent1) & homo (parent2)? I have done filtering for hetero (P1) x homo (P2); homo (P1) x hetero (P2) and hetero (P1) x hetero (P2). After filtering, the total number of SNPs is 1651. Should I consider only these SNPs for mapping RIL population?
> >
> > Please help me with your inputs. I'm doing the analysis for the first time. Also I'm using R first time. I'll highly appreciate your help.
> >
> > I'm attaching my entire data for any help [https://www.dropbox.com/sh/og2pbp7i6c55ljg/AADwovhNmWRKYNK2iHmkwX2oa?dl=0].

> > Regards,

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] Puzzled!! how to filter the data??
messages.body_plain:
Consider that such markers (0.05 MAF) would have extreme segregation distortion in a RIL population. Unless you have reason to believe that SD is real and worth studying in your population, you should probably cull all markers with substantial SD. In a RIL, this might be MAF <= 0.25.

messages.subject: modle for phenotype with four levels
messages.subject_clean: modle for phenotype with four levels
messages.body_plain:
Dear Karl,

I recently want to map a phenotype which includes A, B, C and D four levels. The phenotypes are like, for example, leaves with only red spots, leaves with yellow spots, leaves with both types of spots and leaves with no spots. I looked up in the book of r/qtl that you wrote, and I am confused which model I should used in QTL mapping. It is not the normal distributing phenotype (not continuous), but also not binary. I also don't think that my phenotypes fit in two-part model, right? So do you think whether I can use nonparametric model for mapping? If so, how should I change my phenotype into numeric?

Thank you very much!

Ziming

messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] modle for phenotype with four levels
messages.body_plain:
I'd recommend converting it to a set of binary traits and mapping those, one at a time.

Methods for mapping nominal categorical traits have been described, but nothing along these lines have been implemented in R/qtl.

karl

Finally sat down to look at this.

The write.cross function with format="mapqtl" is currently quite restrictive, in that it can only handle certain segregation types:
1:2:3:4, 1:10;4, 1:10:11:14:4, 2:3:9, 12:13:2:3:9, 5:6, 7:8

(In the code, see https://github.com/kbroman/qtl/blob/master/R/write.cross.mq.R#L76-L163)

So because your first marker has a single genotype "7" and otherwise 1:2:3:4, the data can't be written in mapqtl format by this function.

karl

> On Mar 4, 2017, at 1:20 PM, John Lovell <johnt...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> FYI - This problem comes from the data having all 4 genotypes AC, AD, BC, BD, and a few partially missing A-, B-, -C, -D.
> Since my data is mostly complete, I can get around this via:
>
> > for(chr in chrnames(cross_2write)) cross_2write$geno[[chr]]$data[cross_2write$geno[[chr]]$data>4]<-NA
>
>
> On Friday, February 24, 2017 at 5:48:53 PM UTC-6, John Lovell wrote:
> Hi Karl,
> I am dealing the the same issue as Federico:
> ...
> write.cross(bad4way, filestem = "~/Downloads/bad4way", format = "mapqtl") Error: unrecognized segregation type at marker Chr01K_1008832
> ...
> Chr01K_1008832 is the 1st marker on the 1st chromosome and has a segregation pattern with the next marker that looks like this:
> > table(g2[,1], g2[,2])
>       1   2   3   4   7
>   1 117   1   2   0   1
>   2   3  94   0   3   0
>   3   2   1 101   4   0
>   4   0   1   1  99   0
>   5   0   0   1   0   0
>
> It seems that my genotype data is in order (I can pull together a map etc.), but clearly it isn't. I have spent a bunch of time trying to troubleshoot and can't figure it out. All markers in this population are ABxCD, phase-known with all four genotypes represented. Coding follows the read.cross guidelines, using this dictionary:
>
> matrix(c(NA,"--",
>                  1, "AC",
>                  2, "BC",
>                  3, "AD",
>                  4, "BD",
>                  5 , "A-",
>                  6 , "B-",
>                  7 , "-C",
>                  8 , "-D"), ncol = 2, byrow=T)
>
> I'm attaching an .rda file with of the 1st chromosome in case you can make some time to have a look.
> Any help is appreciated.
> John
>
>
>
>
>
> On Thursday, June 25, 2015 at 7:06:29 AM UTC-5, Karl Broman wrote:
> write.cross with format="mapqtl" only works for phase-known 4-way cross data.
>
> Your call to read.cross isn't really working properly. The genotypes vector for a 4-way cross needs to be a specific list of genotype codes, corresponding to these:
> 1 = AC, 2 = BC, 3 = AD, 4 = BD,
> 5 = A = AC or AD, 6 = B = BC or BD, 7 = C = AC or BC, 8 = D = AD or BD,
> 9 = AC or BD, 10 = AD or BC,
> 11 = not AC, 12 = not BC, 13 = not AD, 14 = not BD
>
> So the data object in R is not really what you want, and while it thinks this is a 4-way cross, R/qtl can't convert it into the MapQTL format.
>
> karl
>
> > On Jun 25, 2015, at 3:27 AM, Federico Calboli <f.ca...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > Hi All,
> >
> > I am trying to use R/qtl to export some data to mapQTL format (no, it is not for me, I'd just use R/qtl). In any case, I have data for an F1/F2 (309 F2 + the 2 F1, which are the two last lines of data). I have the data in 'csv' format, and I can read it in without a single problem by doing:
> >
> > dat = read.cross(format = 'csv', dir = '.', 'f1f2.csv', na.strings = 'NA', genotypes = c('AA','AC','AG','AT','CC','CG','CT','GG','GT','TT'), alleles=c('A','C','G','T'), estimate.map = FALSE)
> >
> > Unfortunately when I try to export it
> >
> > write.cross(dat, format = 'mapqtl', filestem = 'HB', chr = 1, digits = NULL)
> >
> > I get
> >
> > Error: unrecognized segregation type at marker 24319 on chromosome 1
> >
> > (there is at least 1 marker R/qtl does not like in every chromosome). I suspect that I might need to specify that the last 2 individuals are the F1 male and female. Alternatively I might have to remove them... In any case I'd be obliged if you could suggest what I can do to get the export done and over with...
> >
> > Cheers
> >
> > Federico

messages.subject: Map visualization
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am currently using R/QTL to construct genetic map through our university High Performance Computing system. HPCC is not good at visualization work, so I could only get the text results with marker positions on each chromosome such as:
 S3B_PART1_10392228  S3B_PART1_10678203  S3B_PART1_10393475  S3B_PART1_19083996
            0.00000             0.00001             0.00002            13.44919
 S3B_PART1_17809198  S3B_PART1_19113895  S3B_PART1_19083997  S3B_PART1_19083951
           13.88701            13.88702            13.88703            13.88704

I am wondering is there any software to simply visualize my map results without constructing it again.

Thank you!
Yuanwen

Then move it back to your local machine and load with load() or readRDS().
